items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: That's what Mingus' whole thing was. MS. : It's still the same way. Yeah. So Mingus Amos was up there and Arnett...

ctx.x: We had what they called, they defined it and nicknamed it a 'Rump Sale' and they decided on a name that The Jazz Artists give. They were against something about Wein Lorillard, George and Loreli, you know, the owners of the Newport Festival -- excluding certain groups, you know. If you weren't in the 'in' groups, you didn't get a chance to play Newport. That's what Mingus' whole thing was. MS. : It's still the same way.

Yeah. So Mingus Amos was up there and Arnett, and he had a cite called the Cliffwalk Manor, a beautiful hotel right there overlooking the beaches and whatnot, the big grounds where they had tents set up, and we were playing, all day having our little thing and charging admission to get in, and it was beautiful.
